pr_title: Fix Pathfollow direction and add Z forward option
pr_body:
Fixes #53837.

The direction is changed, but some countermeasures are planned in the near future. See #72843, #72795 and #72753.

~~As long as #72843 will be merged, the change about the direction is not breaks compat. However, the following method changes are breaks compat.~~ merged into this PR.

---
PathFollow2D:
- ~~Rename: `rotates` `set_rotates` `is_rotating` -> `rotation_enabled` `set_rotation_enabled` `is_rotation_enabled`~~
- Remove: `lookahead` the DEAD PROPERTY💀

PathFollow2D/3D:
- ~~Rename: `cubic_interp` `set_cubic_interpolation` `get_cubic_interpolation` -> `cubic_interpolation_enabled` `set_cubic_interpolation_enabled` `is_cubic_interpolation_enabled`~~

~~But, to avoid breaking the scene, old methods is made migratable as deprecated in `_set()` `_get()`.~~
pr_comments: I am supporting this, and this is a local change.

Rebased to follow #76082. The prerequisite is to merge #76082 first, since it contains links to class references added in #76082.

Also, for the same reasons as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/74190#issuecomment-1546352973, I have changed to keep the bound method names for compatibility although the function names have been changed for consistency in cpp.
For the record, renaming method arguments is probably breaking compat too (for C# at least?)

> For the record, renaming method arguments is probably breaking compat too (for C# at least?)

That's true, but I think we've already renamed a lot of method arguments in 4.1 already. If we want to preserve this level of compatibility for C# (I personally think it's too demanding), we'd need another dedicated compatibility system for it.
Yeah, I agree. Just mentioning it so it's clear to anyone looking through the changes.

issue_context.title: Path/PathFollow (+Z) wrong orientation
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v3.3.4.stable.official [faf3f883d]

### System information

Ubuntu 21.04

### Issue description

The

```
Path
  - PathFollow
```

Setup orients on `+Z`, inverse from the convention. E.g. `Vector3.FORWARD` is `Vector3(0, 0, -1)` and `look_at()` orients on `-Z`, but `Path/PathFollow` orients on `+Z`.

See: 
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5bc0e4081bbfa077567e1d94b760f81c63eb3392/scene/3d/path_3d.cpp#L120
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5bc0e4081bbfa077567e1d94b760f81c63eb3392/scene/3d/path_3d.cpp#L128

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create the following tree:

```
Path
  - PathFollow
```

2. Set `PathFollow -> Rotation Mode` to `Oriented`.

---

Notice that `+Z` points forward on the curve. It should be `-Z`.

![Screenshot from 2021-10-15 15-53-18](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1177508/137489932-96759b8a-bf4a-40d0-8643-2fe042384f65.png)

### Minimal reproduction project

_No response_
comments: Fixing this will break compatibility with existing projects, so a new property needs to be added in `3.x` to invert the Z direction. (We don't need such a property in `master`.)
@Calinou since it's breaking compatibility maybe we should set milestone of this issue to 4.0?

was just about to post this. I also find it odd that look_at Forward don't have a angle of 0 when using angle_to(). Makes me think what is currently RIGHT should be forward or angle 0 should be at the top. Probably wont happen because ages of convention. But if it were up to me I'd align those somehow.  I'd probably make the trig functions follow the same convention as a clock. That way forward is 0 and the first quadrant is still positive for both sin and cos.

review_comments: These changes seem unrelated to adding a new model front mode to `look_at`. I'm not sure why not split these changes into a separate PR.

I talked to @akien-mga earlier and got his agreement that these method names are bad, but he seems to have a terrible aversion to changing method names in 4.x, so I decided to change only the cpp function names same as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/74190#issuecomment-1546352973. Binding method names have not been changed. If he does not like it, I will split it.
